waves.name: Reader side of the master file
waves.rationale: READJOB runs PGMR, which only reads SPARQ.TEST.MASTER and writes nothing shared. The wave boundary is the dataset, which the extractor marks as an articulation point. The legacy writer keeps producing the file, so the port can be tested against real legacy output and rolled back by running the legacy job. This is a sound first wave only as a toolchain proof. PGMR uses no field it reads and prints nothing, so the wave has almost no business value and the only observable behavior is the return code.
waves.unblocks: Wave 2. It gives the writer port a ported consumer that decodes the record, and it fixes one shared schema for the file. Otherwise it is a chore.

waves.name: Writer of the master file
waves.rationale: WRITEJOB runs PGMW, which writes SPARQ.TEST.MASTER, the file PGMR reads. It moves last because the reader is already ported by then and the contract can be held constant from the wave 1 side. The contract edge is medium confidence: the writer uses LAYOUTX and the reader uses LAYOUTY. Field by field they are byte compatible, but nothing enforces that. The JCL also sets LRECL=80 against a 15 byte layout, which the extractor cannot compare (inference). Confidence is not high for those reasons and because no scheduler was supplied.
waves.unblocks: Retirement of the legacy writer and of the duplicate layout copybook. It is the wave that closes the file contract.
